title: 7.6 A 2.06pJ/b 106.25Gb/s PAM-4 Receiver with 3-Tap FFE and 1-Tap Speculative DFE in 28nm CMOS
problem: High-speed serial links face channel loss (>20dB) requiring equalization; ADC-based receivers offer flexible DSP but consume excessive power at >16nm nodes. RX FFE approaches improve timing margins but increase AFE noise, degrading bit-error-rate.
motivation: Data center I/O bandwidth scaling demands power-efficient 100+ Gb/s serial links with multi-tap equalization to compensate severe channel loss.
method: The receiver uses three tunable signal-processing stages (3-tap RX FFE, which adaptively cancel channel distortion) to create a target pulse pattern (1+0.50: main signal plus a half-strength echo) for a one-tap speculative decision-feedback stage (which predicts bits ahead of time to reduce delay). This recovers from 21.2dB of signal loss without requiring the transmitter to pre-process the signal (no TX FFE). The design separates the cancellation stages from the feedback stage to avoid timing conflicts, eliminates the first intersymbol interference (h1: the strongest echo from prior bits), and maintains power efficiency using mostly-analog circuits.
key_novelty: The core idea is using three receiver-side processing stages to generate a 1+0.50 pulse response for a speculative decision-feedback stage, which eliminates transmitter-side processing while maintaining power efficiency.
contributions: 3-tap RX FFE adaptively generating 1+0.50 response for speculative DFE
21.2dB channel loss compensation without TX FFE
Avoids stringent DFE timing constraints through mixed-signal approach
primary_theme: Energy-efficient PAM-4 receiver with adaptive FFE/DFE for high-loss channels
